title: Queues and backpressure
summary: Queues buffer work, while backpressure limits incoming work when consumers cannot keep up.
overview: Consumer acknowledgements track processing progress, and prefetch limits bound unacknowledged deliveries. A queue alone cannot absorb sustained overload indefinitely; admission limits or shedding must bound backlog.
why: Unbounded waiting turns a traffic spike into long delays and resource exhaustion.
example: Image workers acknowledge completed jobs, cap in-flight deliveries, and reject new submissions when the oldest queued job exceeds the service’s delay budget.
judgment: Decide backlog limits, delivery guarantees, and how failed jobs leave the retry cycle.
next: At peak arrival rates, how long until queue age exceeds the promised completion time?
